races.name: Think Print & Design Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a poor recent form string of PPP and a tendency to fade in the finish; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps on weight, but as a true hold-up type squeezed into a crowded midfield in this 16-runner field, finding a clear run will be a significant challenge given the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle
runners_data.note: Gerard O'Leary's six-year-old showed ability when second over hurdles on Good ground at 2m2f and has genuine form credentials here; a natural rear-of-field operator who is shifted toward midfield by the sheer volume of hold-up horses, though his class (1W2P on sim going) means a clean passage could make him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Storm Eric
runners_data.note: Jamie Flynn sends this seven-year-old into a hurdle maiden after a flat career of placed efforts on Standard ground, making the switch to turf and jumping entirely uncharted; 133 days off the track adds to the query marks, but his best form shows consistency at 10f on the flat and he could settle well in midfield if the jumping comes naturally.

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's four-year-old has run consistently in the 4s over hurdles on Good ground, suggesting a genuine consistent type; a true hold-up horse by nature whose chance is tempered by having to race further forward than ideal in this field, though four runs on similar going (13/14) give confidence in his stamina for this trip.

runners_data.name: Champagne Diamond
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old returning after a massive 368-day absence with only one run on sim going to reference (10th at 2m2f Good); the unknown style tag and that lengthy layoff make him very difficult to assess, and a tendency to fade compounds the concern in what will be an honestly run race.

runners_data.name: Drumconnor Hill
runners_data.note: Cian Collins' five-year-old has three runs on Good ground this summer and shown modest form (7th, 4th, 8th); genuine hold-up horse by nature who is pushed toward a midfield berth here, and his recent form string P2-847 points to a horse that has found little when the pressure is on.

runners_data.name: Kingston Silver
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for W J Lanigan but there is no form on record and going preference is completely unknown; a complete unknown quantity — impossible to assess pace style, stamina or going suitability, making this purely speculative.

runners_data.name: Langage Du Large
runners_data.note: P J Breen's five-year-old has not run for 453 days and fell on its only recorded run; entirely unknown style and going preference makes any assessment guesswork, and the combination of a long absence and a previous fall over hurdles is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old is one of two confirmed front-runners and Jack Kennedy's booking is significant; consistent on Good ground (9/11 on sim going, 0W3P), has placed at this trip three times, and her chance hinges on whether she can control the pace against Rosenborg and hold on once headed.

runners_data.name: Rosenborg
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's five-year-old is the second confirmed front-runner and was second over 2m2f on Good ground last time; Mr Sugrue's 7lb claim helps but this horse has been 12th and 7th in subsequent runs, and the key question is whether he can sustain the gallop past halfway or whether he cedes to Penny Express early.

runners_data.name: Sum Story
runners_data.note: Another Rothwell runner, this five-year-old has run once on similar going (10th at 2m3f Good) and fades in the finish; 54 days since last run is unremarkable, and as a hold-up horse in a field full of them, getting competitive from the rear is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Tell Me See
runners_data.note: John Burke's five-year-old has run twice on Good ground — 8th and 9th — and carries a finish-fade flag; 14 days since last run is fresh enough, but there is nothing in the form to suggest a hold-up horse who fades can overcome this field shape.

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old represents the strongest trainer in terms of recent form (4/30 in 14 days) and Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant jockey booking; placed (3rd, 4th) on Good ground over 2m4f, he is a natural hold-up horse whose best form comes in staying tests, and this 2m1f trip on an honest pace could suit a horse who travels well in midfield.

runners_data.name: Run For Power
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' six-year-old returns after 306 days off the track having been 4th and 12th in two hurdle runs on Good ground; a true hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield by necessity, and the lengthy absence combined with a lack of form makes this a very speculative runner.

runners_data.name: You Lift Me Up
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's four-year-old has one run on record — 11th at 2m1f on Good ground — and carries a fade-in-finish flag; without a jockey listed publicly and just the one poor run to assess, this is one of the most opaque profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Ribadora
runners_data.note: Eoin McCarthy's four-year-old has form of 7th, 5th and 13th over hurdles on Good ground; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who is pushed into a midfield role by the race shape, and a progressive form sequence that ends in a 13th (2m2f Good) does not inspire confidence in this competitive 16-runner maiden.

races.paceDynamic: Penny Express and Rosenborg are the two confirmed front-runners in this 16-runner maiden hurdle, and with both likely to push forward from the flag, an honest, contested gallop is expected throughout the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Wexford. Penny Express, trained by Gordon Elliott and ridden by Jack Kennedy, has the stronger profile of the two and is likely to edge control, but Rosenborg won't surrender the lead cheaply, meaning the pace should be genuine rather than dawdling. This field carries a significant volume of hold-up horses — Plastic Paddy, Sea Eagle, Earthwatch, Drumconnor Hill, Run For Power and Ribadora are all true hold-up types mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field cannot physically accommodate them all — with Sea Eagle, Earthwatch and Tomthescaffolder among those best placed to secure a realistic prominent-to-midfield berth. A genuinely run race over a flat Irish track on Good ground suits prominent racers who can travel smoothly in the slipstream of the pace and quicken at the second-last; pure hold-up horses are disadvantaged by a crowded midfield-to-rear that dilutes their late impact.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Penny Express and Rosenborg fight for the lead and sustain a genuine gallop, tiring the field from the front.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a punishing tempo that stretches the field early, leaving those racing just off the pace in the best position to pounce from two out; horses who travel smoothly in second or third position conserve enough energy to quicken on the Good ground when rivals are emptying.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Penny Express establishes an uncontested lead after Rosenborg fails to sustain the pace or drops away early.
scenarios.body: With Penny Express allowed to bowl along at a controlled tempo under Jack Kennedy, the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and stamina rather than raw pace; Elliott's runner, consistent in Good-ground form and carrying only 158lbs, could simply outslay a field of unproven maiden hurdlers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to set up a strong late run for a horse who finds clear air from the rear of the midfield group.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up horses face a crowded passage problem in a 16-runner field, but a horse like Sea Eagle or Storm Eric who gets a clean run from off the pace could produce a powerful late surge if the front-runners have gone too hard; the Good ground keeps the surface fair for late closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition — Fallers/Pullers
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or early pullers disrupt the pace picture and scramble the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners in a maiden hurdle containing several inexperienced and lightly raced horses, a messy race with interference or a key front-runner coming down could gift an unlikely winner; Kingston Silver and Langage Du Large are unknown quantities whose form is unreadable, making them speculative beneficiaries of chaos.

watchPoints.text: Penny Express and Rosenborg will likely clash for the lead from the start — if Rosenborg refuses to give way, the tempo could become dangerously strong and burn out both front-runners before two out, opening the race for anything tracked in third or fourth.

Sea Eagle is a genuine hold-up horse operating out of his natural role in a 16-runner field; if he gets shuffled back into traffic in the early stages he may never get a clear run, but if Thomas O'Connor (7) can find a position just off the pace, his Good-ground form makes him a live threat.

Tomthescaffolder's Darragh O'Keeffe booking for De Bromhead is notable — watch for this horse being sent forward earlier than his natural hold-up style suggests, as the trainer/jockey combination may try to exploit the pace scenario by positioning closer to the action.

Kingston Silver and Langage Du Large are completely unknown quantities with no assessable form — both are capable of causing interference or being involved in jumping mishaps that disrupt the race shape, particularly significant in a 16-runner maiden hurdle on the first circuit.

The Rothwell yard runs three horses (Rosenborg, Sum Story, You Lift Me Up) — if Rosenborg is used as a pacemaker to soften the race for a stablemate, Sum Story or You Lift Me Up could be the intended beneficiary, though the form of all three is modest.

races.name: Treo Eile Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong record on Good ground (11 from 15 placed in similar conditions), won 16f on Good recently and ran well here 16 days ago — consistent profile that suits tracking the pace here and challenging late; headgear worn (p) suggests needs holding together.
runners_data.comment: Chosen Shant arrives on the back of a second last time out and a winner two starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going; carrying 168 lb is the one query, but she heads this 17-runner field as the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a T14 runner in the yard (1 from 1); has placed on Good ground before but recent form shows struggles in big fields, and a 28-day break may require him to show more freshness than his 8603-0 string suggests.
runners_data.comment: Eaglewood shaped with promise when third two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before at a testing 165 lb; the concern is she has been winless in her last five starts, and her unplaced effort since that third needs improvement.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Hold-up style for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy, a pairing that commands respect even in a modest handicap; has five runs on Good or similar without a win or place but is only five years old and the step back from softer may help.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pull-up and a fall among recent outings, Tropical Twist carries a hefty 163 lb and has a trainer badly out of form at 1/44 over the past fortnight; she has run over today's trip and going before, but there is plenty working against her here.

runners_data.name: Teagarden Jazz
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who hasn't run for 83 days and has a poor record on Good ground (13 from 15 placed in similar conditions but never winning); tongue-tie noted, and Charlie Keegan's yard is cold at present — significant questions here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulling up two back is a concern, but she has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 105 ranks her second of 17 — the main risk is reproducing that pulled-up effort under 161 lb after 83 days off.

runners_data.name: Backwithyourown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed a clear second-place effort on Good ground over 16f in this trip range; Wexford-regular trainer John Burke and Eoin Walsh partnership is competent but the 0 from 12 record on Good going is a worry despite the form.
runners_data.comment: Backwithyourown arrives here 28 days fresh, with experience of today's distance and going working in her favour, but she's winless in her last five starts and that unseating incident lurks in the recent record; a second four starts back offers some encouragement, though 160 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, wearing a hood (p) for Ian Donoghue's yard; going OK and trip fine, but career pattern of fading from front positions (form 89-245) may leave her vulnerable if her gallop is not perfectly judged — key runner regardless.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Annarubyrose does hold a second three starts back to her name, though fifth and fourth in more recent outings suggest she's knocking without quite breaking through; experience over today's trip and going at least removes those unknowns under 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fitted with a tongue-tie for Edward Power; 14 days since last run and ran 14 days before that — trainer keeping her busy, which can indicate a horse on the upgrade, but has not placed in 5 starts and Conor Smithers takes a 7lb claim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up most recently, Tudorista faces an uphill task off 157 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form isn't impossible at a rating of 90.

runners_data.name: Tellmemamema
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been placed three times in the last six starts on Good ground and is steadily improving through the handicap ranks; Kieren Buckley an experienced handler of these types, and the horse carries the hood (p) — worth respect if the pace does collapse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tellmemamema has been going the wrong way with fifth two starts back and fourth three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going; the 152 lb burden is a stiff ask for a mare yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Erne Star
runners_data.note: 955 days absent — this is an enormous question mark regardless of profile; genuine hold-up type pushed toward midfield by the redistribution, so the style fit is compromised on top of a near three-year break, and the form figures (9000/) tell their own story.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for over 950 days, Erne Star faces a stiff task on return, ranked 13th of 17 on our figures; has run over today's trip, but the lengthy layoff makes her hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose recent form (P809-0) makes grim reading; Paul Flynn's yard has had a runner in the last fortnight, and while she races off a low mark of 77, being forced closer to midfield than her natural style dictates further diminishes her chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up and two unplaced efforts among recent outings, Lady Victrix cuts a difficult profile — ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, carrying 147 lb, and with a trainer hitting just 5% over the past fortnight, there is little obvious encouragement despite going experience.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose best efforts on Good ground have come when able to settle — being pushed toward midfield by the sheer volume of closers in this field means she cannot race to her natural rhythm; form figures (PP-068) suggest she is finding her feet but not yet competitive enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two pulls-up among them, Wings Of Africa faces a stiff task carrying 145 lb and ranked near the foot of our figures; familiarity with today's going is slim consolation for a mare in such ragged form.

runners_data.name: Stormy Jenn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with a 'fades in finish' flag; her best placed effort was on Heavy and she's ridden by a 7lb claimer — the redistribution away from her natural rear position hurts, and her recent form (63P-F0) gives little encouragement even in a weak heat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 17 on our figures, Stormy Jenn's recent profile — unplaced, a fall, and a pull-up — makes her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going, and a third four starts back offers a faint glimmer.

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed twice on Good ground (3rd and 2nd from 15 runs in similar conditions) and is trained by Rothwell alongside Maxios Lady; Shane O'Callaghan takes a 3lb claim which helps, and this is the closest to a genuine closer who can still physically make a run from the position she's likely to occupy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, Avandra faces a stiff task, with a trainer in the depths of a lean spell (1 from 26 in the last fortnight); she has run over today's trip and going before, but that's faint consolation here.

runners_data.name: La Rocca Lass
runners_data.note: 109 days between runs and a form string of 90000- makes for concerning reading; a true hold-up type fitted with a tongue-tie and ridden by a 7lb claimer, and a tendency to fade in the finish compounds the difficulty of racing out of her natural style here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 109 days, La Rocca Lass arrives short of recent encouragement, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 89 suggests some unexposed ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Maxios Lady
runners_data.note: 315 days off the track and a form string of 000P- — Rothwell runs both this and Avandra, and this is clearly the second string; another hold-up type pushed toward midfield and carrying the 'fades in finish' flag, making this a very difficult race to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulled up most recently, Maxios Lady returns after a 315-day absence for a yard firing at just 4% — she has plenty to prove before asking for confidence here.

runners_data.name: Game Phoenix
runners_data.note: Top-rated hold-up horse in the field (OR=97) with four placed efforts and class ceiling above most rivals; has been off 70 days and recent figures (330-97) suggest a resurgence in form, but no jockey listed is a notable concern, and racing closer to midfield than naturally desired limits the scenario in which she wins.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Prominent type with one win from nine runs and three places on Good or similar; 77 days since last run and no trainer form in the past 14 days, but showed a solid fourth on Good over 20f recently — distance step back to 17f may actually sharpen her up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Annie Agnew nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 104 marks her out as a leading threat in a 17-runner field. Carrying 165 lb is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Annarubyrose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 17 and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, she should stride into an uncontested role from the off on Good ground at Wexford, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m1f. Chosen Shant, Eaglewood, Backwithyourown, and Annie Agnew will press forward into prominent positions just behind her, creating a compact early order but not a pressured one — the pace is unlikely to be searingly fast. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally; Lady Victrix, Erne Star, Wings Of Africa, Stormy Jenn, Avandra, La Rocca Lass, and Maxios Lady are all genuine closers redistributed toward midfield on the map because they cannot all settle at the rear in a 17-runner field — the more likely beneficiaries of prominent berths behind Annarubyrose are those with a genuine record of racing handy. A controlled pace set by a single front-runner on Good ground over this trip at Wexford will typically compress the field and reward horses racing in the first four or five — prominent racers who can travel into the race and pounce from a handy position hold the decisive tactical advantage here, with pure hold-up types at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Annarubyrose Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Annarubyrose is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a fair but not punishing gallop and the prominent pack never seriously pressures her.
scenarios.body: Annarubyrose dictates fully from the front, controls the tempo, and gives a late flourish on the run-in having conserved energy; the horses best placed to challenge are those who tracked her closely from the outset rather than those who tried to close from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Presser Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a handy-travelling prominent racer tracks the leader comfortably through the race and delivers a well-timed challenge at the last.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable pace set, a horse travelling with the early leaders can quicken off the bridle at the second-last and overhaul Annarubyrose on the run-in; this scenario rewards horses with tactical speed and a sound record on Good ground who race off a patient hold just behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Pack Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly quicker than expected and the leading group begins to tire from the third-last, opening gaps for a well-positioned midfield horse to thread through.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting in fifth to eighth in the early stages uses the gaps that open as the leaders tie up, arriving with a sustained run from two out; Game Phoenix, despite a poor recent run, has the class ceiling and a profile that suits closing ground on Good, while Tropical Twist and Avandra could also make progress from similar positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace develops into a genuine test and a string of prominent horses fade, creating enough clear air for a genuine hold-up horse to land a late blow.
scenarios.body: This is an unlikely outcome given the single-paced nature of the gallop and the number of hold-up types forced out of their natural rear position, meaning most closers will be unable to build the momentum they need; Avandra has placed twice on Good and is the most capable of the genuine closers if the shape somehow does collapse.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of the prominent pack — Chosen Shant, Eaglewood, or Annie Agnew — pushes up to seriously pressure Annarubyrose in the first mile, because if they do the pace lifts materially and the race shape changes entirely.

Annarubyrose's hood and front-running role make her the axis of the race — if she gets first run turning for home and is still travelling, she is hard to catch; watch her position at the third-last as the critical indicator.

Game Phoenix (OR=97, no jockey declared) is the class horse in the field on ratings and has shown upward momentum — any market move once the jockey is confirmed should be taken seriously given the unexplained absence.

Erne Star's 955-day absence is a serious flag; watch how she is ridden from the outset — if she jumps and travels, Francis Casey may have her significantly fitter than the long layoff implies, but expect her to find little.

With 17 runners on Good ground and a tight Wexford circuit, watch for traffic incidents from the second-last as the midfield compresses — horses like Avandra and Tropical Twist who are well-placed could be hampered if the race bunches.

races.name: Neville Hotels Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gerard O'Leary who arrives in good nick just 11 days after his last run; his OR-129 is the joint highest in the race and his Good-ground handicap form is solid, though his best recent figures have come over slightly longer trips and he will need an end-to-end gallop to unlock his finishing kick from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Jabbar arrives here on the back of a consistent run of form — a winner one start back, then placed second and third in succession before a fourth last time out, and he has experience of today's distance and going. The 11-day turnaround looks sharp enough, and his 133 rating marks him as the one to beat under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Mode Avion
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and his style fits a solo lead perfectly, but his STYLE_FIT tag flags he is effectively operating out of his most comfortable role here — he has not led and won at this level before, and 101 days off the track adds uncertainty to whether he can sustain the gallop into the final flight.|
runners_data.comment: Mode Avion boasts a second and a win in his last five starts, has run over today's trip, and a rating of 130 sees him rank second of eight — a genuine threat. The concern is his trainer's dire recent form at 1/44, and he returns after 101 days off.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old is a hold-up type fresh off an 18-day break, with ten runs on Good ground in his history returning a modest 1W-3P from 15 applicable runs; Daniel King takes the ride and Tassarolo's record over this 2m1f trip at Good is workmanlike rather than dominant.|
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo brings a lively recent profile — a winner two starts back and a winner four starts back, with a second three starts back too — and he handles today's distance and going, making him a genuine threat; the key risk is bouncing back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe partners this Henry De Bromhead seven-year-old who has a 2W-3P record from 11 relevant Good-ground runs — the strongest similar-going profile in the field; she fell on her most recent start but prior to that won at OR-level and has the prominent style to sit ideally in the slipstream of Mode Avion, making her a natural fit for the dominant race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Fell on her latest start is the obvious concern, but she showed real ability when winning three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 154 lb is a stiff ask, though her rating of 119 suggests she retains solid claims if she bounces back.

runners_data.name: Shaboozee
runners_data.note: J.J. Slevin takes over for Joseph O'Brien on this five-year-old who has been off the track for 316 days — a significant absence flag; his 2W-2P from eight comparable Good-ground runs is strong when fit, and his prominent style suits the expected shape, but the long layoff makes his readiness the key variable.|
runners_data.comment: Shaboozee won twice in his last five starts, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims here; the concern is a 316-day absence, which makes his return to action the one question mark over his participation.

runners_data.name: Now So Jake
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's eight-year-old is a true front-runner by inclination who has been absent for 736 days, a huge stamina-for-form concern; the field's prominent congestion means he is unlikely to secure his natural berth, and both the lengthy layoff and the style dislocation combine to make him a significant risk at face value.|
runners_data.comment: A 736-day absence makes Now So Jake enormously difficult to assess, and ranked seventh of eight on our figures the task of recommending him is harder still. Three wins in his last five starts and going experience offer faint encouragement, but the layoff is the overwhelming concern.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Eoin Griffin's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who ran just nine days ago and has the benefit of recent race fitness; his blinkers are retained and his one win in similar going came from off the pace, but his OR-113 is the lowest in the field and his back-to-back runs at this course have been modest, making him vulnerable on raw class.|
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before flopping last time out, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the 150 lb burden is a stern ask, however, and her recent form is inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.note: John McConnell's four-year-old ran nine days ago and brings a hood — a horse who wants to race prominently but simply cannot get there in a field stacked with rivals for that position; his recent SOF/GOO form shows promise but two attempts at 2m+ on Good ground have returned only a fourth and a tenth, and his redistribution to a mid-pack role he does not suit is a meaningful discount.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures and representing a trainer without a winner in 31 attempts over the past fortnight, Wonderfulwonderful is hard to fancy despite her recent win four starts back; unplaced last time out and shouldering 148 lb, experience over today's trip and going is about all she offers here.

races.paceDynamic: Mode Avion is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural challenger pressing from the outside, should settle into a comfortable, owner-controlled lead at a sustainable Good-ground gallop over this 2m1f trip. Ma Belle Etoile, Shaboozee, and Wonderfulwonderful all carry genuine prominent intentions but the shape cannot accommodate all of them at the fore — Shaboozee and Ma Belle Etoile have the stronger credentials and recent form to actually secure those berths, while Wonderfulwonderful and Now So Jake are true prominent types who will likely be shuffled wider into a mid-pack position they do not naturally inhabit. Jabbar and Splashing Out are the genuine hold-up operators, with Tassarolo also tracking from the rear, meaning the closing kick in the final quarter-mile will be well contested but launched from further back than those runners prefer. This race shape — one honest front-runner, a small cluster of prominent types just off the pace, and a light late-charge brigade — strongly favours the prominent-to-handy profile that can sit within a length or two of Mode Avion through the final turn and pounce approaching the last, rewarding horses who travel fluently close to the pace rather than those relying on a sustained late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Mode Avion bowls along uncontested and the race is run at a measured, honest gallop that sets it up for the chasers just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ma Belle Etoile and Shaboozee sit in the slipstream of Mode Avion through the final bend and have the luxury of picking their moment, with the steady tempo meaning jumping fluency and tactical position matter more than raw finishing speed; prominent types who travel well on Good ground dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong enough to string out the field and the prominent brigade get into a rhythm that burns them up before the last.
scenarios.body: Jabbar and Tassarolo track the race from the wings and, if the mid-race tempo lifts unexpectedly, arrive with untapped reserves while the prominent horses have flattened out; Jabbar's handicap mark of 129 and Good-ground form gives him the class edge in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Mode Avion is allowed a completely unchallenged, confidence-boosting lead and the field fails to close the gap turning for home.
scenarios.body: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old, carrying the lightest competitive burden of the principals, simply idles in front at his own tempo and the chasers find the margin too great at the last; this scenario demands no tactical pressure whatsoever and a clean round of jumping, both of which are plausible on Good ground at Wexford.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Mode Avion's jumping breaks down early or multiple prominent types crowd each other, creating a ragged, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: Jabbar or Splashing Out, both true hold-up operators, benefit from a messy race where positioning becomes irrelevant and a clean final-flight jump wins it; the disrupted shape neutralises the prominent brigade's advantage and hands the initiative to the patient back-runners.

watchPoints.text: Ma Belle Etoile's jumping deserves close attention — she fell on her last start and if she has any residual hesitation at her hurdles she could cost herself the prominent position that is central to her winning chance in this shape.|

Shaboozee's 316-day absence is the single biggest form unknown in the race — watch his paddock condition and early race behaviour to judge whether Joseph O'Brien has brought him back ready to fire first time up.|

Mode Avion setting the tempo unchallenged is the fulcrum of the whole race shape; if he makes an early jumping error or is unexpectedly challenged by Wonderfulwonderful or Now So Jake forcing their way forward, the controlled lead scenario dissolves entirely.|

Now So Jake and Wonderfulwonderful are both competing for a prominent berth that the race shape cannot give them both — watch the early stages for crowding or pushing between these two and Ma Belle Etoile, which could unsettle the tactical order behind Mode Avion.|

Splashing Out is the freshest of the back-markers having run just nine days ago; watch whether Peter Smithers (7) settles him cleanly in rear, as a hold-up horse who gets shuffled wide or loses his rhythm early will struggle to land a telling blow from OR-113.|

races.name: SIS Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mister Vic
runners_data.note: 8-year-old hold-up horse for Steve Jones who hasn't run in 63 days — a noted tendency to fade in the finish is a concern over 3m, and the 7lb claimer Sean Cleary-Farrell has a challenging task trying to produce him with a finish in a big field; Good ground form is adequate (10/14 similar runs) but the fade flag is damning.
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner four starts back but has been unplaced in his two most recent outings, and 63 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though 168 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: Michael Kenneally (5lb claimer) rides for John McConnell — a naturally prominent runner who has placed five times in his last 15 Good-ground starts without winning, and the extra 3m trip at Wexford on this track may finally suit; headgear (blinkers) indicates he needs holding together early.
runners_data.comment: Charlie's Dilemma has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 107 just edges him ahead of his 16 rivals, but he's winless in his last five starts and comes from a yard without a winner in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: 5-year-old for Simon Cavanagh ridden by 7lb claimer Kevin Healy — has placed at 24f on Good and clearly handles this going well (7 from 9 similar-going runs), and his prominent racing style positions him perfectly just off a genuinely-run pace; the F in recent form is a flag worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third three starts back, Clone Cross has shown ability without a win in his last six starts, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; the main concern is a jumping record that includes a fall and two pull-ups in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Matter Of Opinion
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and cheekpieces suggest a horse that needs niggling along — a hold-up runner whose recent form (P579-7) is uninspiring, and while she handles Good ground adequately, the 3m trip is the longest she has attempted and Ms L A Byrne (7lb) faces a tough ask in a 17-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up five runs back, Matter Of Opinion does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his rating of 102 suggests hidden ability — the concern is that recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on this 5-year-old who has been placed four times on Good ground at 24f — a natural hold-up horse who shows excellent consistency without winning, and Kennedy's positional intelligence could be the key if he can find a clear run in a crowded rear division.
runners_data.comment: Gerrys Wish has been second three times in her last five starts but that pulled-up run lurks in the record, she's yet to win in recent form, and a trainer striking at just 2% is a concern; the trip and going hold no fears, though 161 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for John McConnell, has won off this OR at 26f on Good and carries the visor — will attempt to lead from the front and control tempo, though at 11 years old and on a tight turnaround (26 days), stamina reserves over 3m may be tested late.
runners_data.comment: Tango Theatre showed she can win in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going, but four runs without a win since that victory are hard to ignore, and a trainer without a winner in 31 recent attempts is a significant concern under a hefty 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes over on this 8-year-old for Anthony Mullins — recent form reads poorly (/0P9-8) and the hold-up style in a crowded field over this trip makes it hard to see a route to the winner's enclosure; similar-going record of 0W2P in 15 runs says it all.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, including a pull-up, Glendine Billy brings distance-and-going experience but is up against it from 156 lb; our rating of 96 suggests more ability than recent efforts show, yet the form line gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, won at 24f on Good and has been placed at 26f — Sam Ewing takes the ride and she must fight for the lead from the off; if she secures it cleanly, her frontrunning profile gives her a live chance, but a contested duel with Tango Theatre could flatten her before the straight.
runners_data.comment: Consistent mare who was second last time out and a winner four starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; 156 lb is a stern ask, however, and ranked ninth of seventeen she faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with two wins over 24-25f on Good — has been pushed into a midfield map position because of the overcrowded rear, meaning Alan King (7lb) will struggle to secure his natural deep position; the STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 reflects a real risk he races out of character, which would undermine his chance significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts — including a fall in that sequence — Joe's Turn has run over today's trip and going before, yet a sixth and eighth in more recent outings give little encouragement; the 154 lb burden won't help his cause either.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: 5-year-old with a win and a place on Good at 22-24f for David O'Brien — a true sit-and-wait type whose tongue-strap form suggests he needs a clear passage, but with seven other genuine closers ahead of him on the map, Conor Stone-Walsh faces a near-impossible task delivering him late; STYLE_FIT 0.92 cautions strongly.
runners_data.comment: Set The Tone has the form to catch the eye — a winner last time and second two starts back — but she's ranked 12th of 17 on our figures, and the pulled-up run three starts back is hard to ignore; 150 lb is a stern ask against this field.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: 6-year-old carrying a noted tendency to fade in the finish — this is doubly damaging for a hold-up horse that has been redistributed into midfield in a race where she cannot even get her natural rear position; recent form (89P-9U) on Good ground offers little confidence, and Ross Berry (7lb) has limited ammunition here.
runners_data.comment: Fervida has shown precious little in recent starts — unseating last time out after a pulled up and two ninths in her last five — yet she remains unexposed enough that improvement cannot be ruled out entirely, and 149 lb is a stern ask for a mare still finding her feet.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Another horse tagged with a fade-in-finish flag, compounding the difficulty of a hold-up style that has been squeezed into midfield — recent Good-ground form (5/6 runs) shows 0W1P and the 5-year-old's overall profile does not suggest an unlucky horse waiting to strike; Conor Smithers (7lb) rides.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a fall and two unplaced efforts — Strong Contender finds little encouragement in her recent form, and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures she faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe rides for P J Rothwell — has a recent course-form win at 20f on Good and trainer is 1 from 26 in the last 14 days, suggesting a yard not firing at maximum; a true hold-up type displaced to midfield in the map, though Clever Court's form figures do show more promise than most in this redistributed group.
runners_data.comment: Three pulled-ups in recent starts make Clever Court hard to trust, and a trainer firing at just 4% compounds the concern; he does have experience of today's trip and going, and a win two starts back at least confirms he can cross the line.

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: 9-year-old for J A Berry ridden by Mr J P Berry (7lb) — a hold-up horse dropped to OR 72 whose last 15 Good-ground runs show 0 wins from 10 and best recent finish is third at 24f; the redistribution to midfield suits nobody when the horse's form already struggles to land a blow from a true hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cruisin Susan does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third last time out offers a flicker of hope; however, carrying 140 lb and ranked tenth of seventeen, she faces a stiff ask to convert that recent placed effort into something more.

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: 8-year-old for Cian Collins (trainer 1 from 9 in 14 days) ridden by Reserve 1 — a hold-up type whose last run ended in a dismount (D), and form figures (/60-5D) over 24f on Good are poor; 32 days since last run and a reserve jockey booking add further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Fair Damsel nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at a rating of 100 she shapes as a genuine threat at the weights — though 164 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: 9-year-old mare for S Ryan ridden by Reserve 2 — a naturally prominent runner with a win at 22f on Good and placed three times in last 15 similar-going runs; the reserve jockey is a concern, but her prominent style and solid stamina record make her a shape-compatible runner if the booking is confirmed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up among her recent efforts, Sineads Fancy faces a stiff task ranked 13 of 17 here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days off suggests she arrives fresh, but the recent form makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: The Cobblers Wife
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins' 8-year-old has not run for 86 days and is ridden by Reserve 3 — a genuine hold-up horse whose similar-going record is a meagre 2 from 8, and the lengthy absence combined with a reserve rider and redistribution to midfield means she faces obstacles from every angle before jumping a hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulling up most recently, The Cobblers Wife arrives here 86 days fresh and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures — hard to fancy on any angle, though the step back to the track after that break gives connections something to work with.

races.paceDynamic: Tango Theatre and Mobile Mamma are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner field, and both have clear form records of setting or pressing the pace — they will lock horns from the off over this 3m trip on Good ground at Wexford, creating an honest, sustained gallop rather than any false or dawdling tempo. With Joe's Turn, Set The Tone, Fervida, Strong Contender, Clever Court, Cruisin Susan and The Cobblers Wife all true hold-up types but redistributed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear, the actual back half of the field will be more congested and slower to find clear runs than their natural style would suggest. The two leaders set a genuine pace that, over 3 miles on Good ground, will test stamina thoroughly and expose horses who cannot see out the trip or who are stuck in traffic. This race shape strongly favours genuine prominent racers with proven stamina — horses like Charlie's Dilemma, Clone Cross and Sineads Fancy who can sit just off the pace, travel economically and produce a finish — over the hold-up brigade, who face both a congested midfield and a pace that may not come back to them fast enough in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Prominents Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Theatre and Mobile Mamma set a true, unrelenting gallop and the hold-up horses get tangled in a crowded midfield.
scenarios.body: The two leaders maintain a genuine pace throughout the 3 miles, burning off the rear-division types who cannot get clear in time; horses sitting just off the pace in the prominent group travel smoothly and pounce in the straight. Charlie's Dilemma, Clone Cross and Sineads Fancy — all proven on Good ground and capable of racing prominently — are best placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mobile Mamma or Tango Theatre blows up mid-race and the tempo drops, allowing hold-up horses to cruise into contention.
scenarios.body: A false or uneven gallop over the back gives the genuine hold-up horses a rare chance to travel into the race without expending energy, and the finishing straight becomes a sprint test rather than a stamina examination. Gerrys Wish and Clever Court, who both show strong recent form on Good ground, are best positioned to capitalise if their natural closing style can finally be deployed in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mobile Mamma or Tango Theatre drops away early and one gets a solo lead, controlling tempo entirely.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating at a measured pace can steal a march on a big field where the midfield is overcrowded and rivals struggle to organise a challenge until it is too late. Tango Theatre, an 11-year-old who has won off this OR and handles Good ground well with visor headgear, could be the chief beneficiary of an uncontested lead if Mobile Mamma fails to hold her position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is relentless from flag to finish and most of the field is emptied out before the final flight.
scenarios.body: A true stamina grind over 3 miles on Good ground benefits horses with the highest proven endurance and best recent form figures at the trip; the entire hold-up contingent is neutralised by traffic and fatigue. Gerrys Wish, with four runner-up finishes on Good and Jack Kennedy in the saddle, and Joe's Turn, who has won and placed at 24-26f on Good, represent the stayers best equipped to grind it out if the pace is brutal throughout.

watchPoints.text: Mobile Mamma and Tango Theatre will contest the lead aggressively from the start — watch whether one of them folds before halfway, because a contested duel at the head of a 17-runner field over 3m on Good ground can bring the pace back to midfielders far sooner than expected.

Gerrys Wish, despite Jack Kennedy in the saddle, is a true hold-up horse in an overcrowded rear division — watch how Kennedy manages the first half mile, as a slow break or early traffic could strand him with too much to do from a position he could not get in the first place.

Clone Cross has a Fall (F) in recent form at 24f on Good — in a field of 17 at this pace over 3m, a jumping error from a prominent position would cause significant interference and should be monitored at the early flights.

Clever Court (Darragh O'Keeffe, P J Rothwell) has a recent win on Good and is one of the few redistributed hold-up types with credible form — if the pace suddenly softens mid-race and a clear gap opens on the inside, he is the one among the displaced closers most likely to capitalise.

Reserve jockey bookings on Fair Damsel and Sineads Fancy (Reserves 1 and 2) mean late jockey changes are possible — Sineads Fancy in particular has a prominent style that suits this race shape, so confirmation of her rider is worth tracking before the off.

races.name: Pat Farrell Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Jonny Carrol
runners_data.note: The race-shaping force here — sole front-runner likely to lead from flag to finish at a pace of his own choosing; 5yo in good heart on Good ground, though apprentice claimer Miss Ella Herbison's ability to conserve him correctly on a long-run trip is a legitimate question.
runners_data.comment: Placed third four starts back, Jonny Carrol has struggled since but returns fit on 15 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 109 marks him as the one to beat in this field of 17, even if winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Deise Crystal
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who has placed twice recently on Good ground over shorter; 72-day break is worth monitoring for sharpness, but if Anna McGuinness (7) can slot her into a handy position from the rear, her 17f-19f placings suggest the step to 2m4f could suit.
runners_data.comment: Deise Crystal posted back-to-back minor finishes — third last time out and a second two starts back — and has experience of today's going, giving him strong claims off a 96 official mark; the 72-day absence and 164 lb burden are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Layenda
runners_data.note: Bred and raced as a hold-up type with a flagged tendency to fade late in the finish — the 2m4f trip at a slow pace is not obviously in her favour; four runs on Good ground have returned only one placing and she may again be one-paced when it matters.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a pulled up and a ninth — Layenda does bring going experience to the table and ran third two starts back, but 54 days off the track and a hefty 163 lb burden make her prospects here look limited.

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue in the saddle is a significant booking for a hold-up type with an outstanding record on Good ground (12 of 15 runs), including multiple places over a range of distances; the staying profile over 2m4f suits and Donoghue's tactical nous should compensate for racing slightly out of natural position.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts in recent starts, Bayonetta has back-to-back seconds in her recent form and has run over today's trip and going before — her rating of 100 makes her a leading threat among 17 rivals; the concern is she remains winless in her last five.

runners_data.name: Riverstown Boy
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who is almost certain to secure a front-rank berth close to Jonny Carrol — five consecutive fifth-place finishes show consistency without a win, and the 2m4f distance at Wexford on Good going is a known quantity for him; his stamina at this trip in a pressure race is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to trouble the judge, Riverstown Boy at least returns on a going surface he has encountered before and is fresh enough after 28 days off; carrying 162 lb against a competitive field of 17 will test his ability to improve on that persistent fifth-place pattern.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Has two hurdles wins to her name and a recent second on Good ground at 19f; Peter Smithers (7) is a light-weight booking, and while she settles toward the rear, her winning profile and comfort on this surface give her a live each-way profile in a wide-open bottom half of the race.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in her last four starts overall, Barrogstown Girl has run over today's going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround; the 157 lb burden could be the factor that keeps her from threatening at the finish.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Gift
runners_data.note: A hold-up type whose last three completed runs have all produced seventh or eighth positions on Good ground — the fall and pulled-up entries in recent form add jumping uncertainty; 53 days off and a mid-race tendency to find little in the straight make this a difficult ride for Eoin Walsh.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, with two successive mishaps — a fall then a pulled up — clouding his recent picture; Charlie's Gift has run over today's trip and going, but 157 lb is a stern ask for a gelding whose form is hard to read right now.

runners_data.name: Zaryagle
runners_data.note: Off the track for 292 days and returning cold — even a natural come-from-behind racer like this needs jumping fluency and fitness to make an impact, and the extended absence is a serious concern; good-ground form at 16f shows modest placing potential but the 2m4f trip is untested and the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Rated 104 and ranked second of 17 runners, Zaryagle has run over today's going and is well treated on official ratings — the main concern is his pulling-up last time out after 292 days off, leaving fitness a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Madam Elle
runners_data.note: All five runs in the form book have been on Heavy ground and she has no turf form on anything near Good — this is an entirely unknown surface profile, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the risk; her redistribution into midfield rather than her natural rear position makes her hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 156 days, Madam Elle faces a stiff ask carrying 153 lb, and our rating of 77 ranks her 14th of 17 here — hard to fancy on these figures, though she does have a seventh-place finish to her name.

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: A flagged fader who has posted finishes of 9-8-7-7-0 at a variety of Good-ground trips without threatening — racing outside her natural rear-field comfort zone and carrying a style-fit discount, she needs a significantly stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce to make any impression.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-to-tail-of-field finishes, Notmiwadi is hard to fancy ranked 16 of 17 on our figures; she has run over today's going before, which offers a small crumb of comfort, but the evidence here is against her.

runners_data.name: Itaintmebabe
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained 7yo who has been off 85 days; her one recent win came on Soft ground and Good-ground form has returned only modest placings — the surface switch back to Good is a mild concern, and she carries a style-fit note as a horse pushed into midfield rather than her preferred hold-up berth.
runners_data.comment: Itaintmebabe landed a win four starts back but has been unplaced or out of the frame in his three subsequent runs, and 85 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though 152 lb is a stern weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Who's Da Goose
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 4yo with just three runs, all at shorter than today's 2m4f trip — the stamina question over the extra distance is significant; a natural closer whose redistribution into midfield leaves her racing out of role, and the combination of trip doubt and style displacement makes her hard to assess.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and still open to improvement, Who's Da Goose has been winless in his last three starts but shaped best when fifth of those three; the 28-day break looks a fair freshener, and with only a handful of runs to his name, there is likely more to come at 152lb.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: Veteran 9yo who found a spot of form recently at 18f on Good ground (4th); Donagh Meyler rides a horse whose best runs have come from a patient hold-up position, but at this age and over an extended trip, the step up in runners and being pushed into a more prominent slot than he prefers is a risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sekakarma does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 24 days since his fourth last time out suggests he arrives fresh; however, a pulled up four starts back and that 147 lb burden make it hard to fancy him with conviction.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with one career hurdle win on Good ground and a strong placing record (13 of 15 runs in the frame); Daniel King takes the ride on a horse who has placed three from three at 24f, suggesting the trip is a genuine asset — his style-fit displacement is the main concern but his stamina credentials are real.
runners_data.comment: Hob's Angel has shown she can compete, with a win and a second in recent starts, but ranked 12 of 17 on our figures she faces a stiff task here, and 145 lb adds further to the burden.

runners_data.name: Keep The Head
runners_data.note: Has a flagged fade-in-finish tendency, a P-9-P-P-0 recent form string and a Reserve jockey booking — none of those factors encourage confidence; even mapped into midfield rather than the hold-up position he naturally occupies, he looks among the least likely winners in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and having pulled up on three of those occasions, Keep The Head makes for a difficult proposition here; she does return on a quick turnaround with going experience to her name, but ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with an uninspiring form string of 0-0-0-6-0 and another Reserve jockey booking; his best effort has been a sixth, and while the going is suitable, he remains unexposed at 2m4f and the style-fit discount means he will need to find significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, John Dixen faces a stiff ask here; a sixth two starts back offers slim encouragement, and at least he arrives fit on a 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Last ran just one day ago — that extreme recency is the dominant factor and freshness must be questioned regardless of his 9th-8th-1st-?-13th form profile; the one win at 17f on Good ground shows ability, but the 1d turnaround from his previous engagement is a very unusual flag to carry into a handicap hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has struggled since, posting an eighth and a ninth in his last two — and at just one day since his previous outing, the turnaround is sharp. Has run over today's trip and going, though his ranking of 11th of 17 suggests he faces stiff competition.

races.paceDynamic: Jonny Carrol is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and is expected to bowl along on a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset — no rival is likely to challenge him for the front position on a sustained basis over 2m4f at Wexford. With only Riverstown Boy as a genuine prominent-type likely to sit close to the pace, the early tempo will be controlled and moderate, meaning Jonny Carrol can essentially dictate the rhythm throughout and reach the business end of the race without having been pressured. This field is heavily stacked with hold-up horses — Who's Da Goose, Zaryagle, Notmiwadi, Itaintmebabe, Madam Elle and several others are all natural closers who are redistributed into midfield positions precisely because there is not enough natural pace ahead of them; none of them are true front-runners who will force the issue. The race shape therefore strongly favours horses who can travel prominently close to Jonny Carrol or pick up efficiently from a handy midfield position, as a slow-run race off a lone lead can produce a sprint finish that disadvantages deep closers — particularly those tagged with a tendency to fade late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Jonny Carrol is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a controlled, renewable pace throughout the 2m4f trip.
scenarios.body: Jonny Carrol dictates every yard, conserves energy through the middle section and has enough in reserve to repel challengers at the final hurdle; Riverstown Boy, the only horse likely to track the lead, is ideally placed to pounce if the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Riverstown Boy pushes up aggressively to sit on Jonny Carrol's shoulder and the two grind out a genuinely contested lead, lifting the pace and stretching the field.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop filters the closers and exposes any stayers from the midfield pack; horses with proven stamina and a liking for Good ground who can travel prominently or just off the pace will thrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and a well-positioned midfield runner with a sharp turn of foot picks its way through a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: A moderate early gallop bunches the field, and a horse sitting three or four lengths off the pace with a clean jumping round can accelerate past a tiring leader; Bayonetta's consistent form in similar conditions makes it a candidate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong pace develops and the front two are seriously weakened by the last, allowing the pack of redistributed hold-up horses to run through them.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses like Zaryagle, Who's Da Goose or Notmiwadi to have been quietly cantering in midfield while the leaders burned each other out — plausible in theory but undermined by the fact all three are racing out of their natural role and carry style-fit discounts.

watchPoints.text: Backinabit ran just one day ago — if connections have deliberately double-entered and declared this horse fit, the extremely short turnaround could mask a viability concern or alternatively signal unusual confidence; watch the market closely for support or drifting.

Jonny Carrol faces no genuine pace rival in this 17-runner field — if he is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged at a crawl, the entire race could turn on the final two hurdles and his apprentice rider's ability to judge pace over 2m4f will be pivotal.

Zaryagle returns from a 292-day absence having not run since finishing pulled-up — jumping fluency over hurdles after such a lengthy layoff is a real question in a race this competitive, and could create interference in a densely packed midfield.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Zaryagle, Madam Elle, Notmiwadi, Itaintmebabe, Who's Da Goose and others) will all be jostling for midfield ground rather than settling at the rear — watch the first three hurdles for traffic issues and check positioning as the field settles.

Bayonetta's booking of Keith Donoghue stands out as the most significant jockey upgrade in this race — if Donoghue moves him prominently from the gate rather than sitting deep as the nominal style suggests, that tactical adjustment could reframe the entire race shape.

races.name: Pat Farrell Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here; goes on Good, races in tongue-tie, trainer Eoin Doyle 1/4 in 14 days — should lead uncontested but is officially tagged as a Prominent type racing somewhat out of natural role and that tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a second four starts back, Poppycon brings solid placed form to this race and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 97 marks him out as a leading contender — though he remains winless in recent starts, and that fall three runs back is a concern.

runners_data.name: Chosen Princess
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 88 days off which is a notable absence; handles Good going and stays 2m4f+ judged by recent runs, but trainer strike rate of 0/1 in the 14-day window offers little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and carrying a hefty 163 lb, Chosen Princess nevertheless has experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 92 marks her as a leading threat — though a run of 88 days off the track is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Thurman
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ridden by a 7lb claimer; 105 days since last run is the longest layoff in the field and must be treated with caution, though he does handle Good ground over this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulling up two outings back are clear concerns, though she has run over today's trip and a 105-day break could mean she returns freshened; the 160 lb burden makes improvement hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ballyminnion Boy
runners_data.note: Flags as a hold-up type with a concerning tendency to fade late; form string of FP-008 is poor and he has never placed on Good going across three attempts — hard to find an angle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a fall and a pull-up, Ballyminnion Boy arrives here 28 days later carrying 158 lb with a tough ask ahead; experience over today's going offers some hope, but his recent record gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: Another confirmed fader over the final stages despite placing last time out on Good ground over this trip; tongue-tie applied, trainer 0/3 recently, but the course-distance form is the one positive.|
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying a testing 157 lb, Las Brisas Boy brings distance-and-going experience to this and our rating of 91 marks him out as a serious threat; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent form over 20 furlongs on similar ground is the standout profile in this field; a hold-up horse who has proven he can win this sort of contest but depends on getting clear at the right moment in a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 17 on our figures and carrying a hefty 155 lb, Larinks Lane is hard to fancy despite her two wins in her last five starts — that eighth last time out is the more recent pointer, and a trainer firing at just 4% over the last 14 days adds little confidence, even if she has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose natural position at the rear cannot be guaranteed in this crowded race — style-fit discount applies; form of 070-0P on Good ground gives little confidence and he's only 15 days since last run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up the most recent effort, Davitts Quay faces a stiff task here — ranked 11 of 17 on our figures — though experience on today's going and a run just 15 days ago at least confirm fitness and familiarity with conditions.

runners_data.name: Ballinvasas Best
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a string of fourth-place finishes suggesting he gets into contention without winning; eight-year-old who handles Good ground and handles 2m4f, making him a likely traveller near the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Ballinvasas Best has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days since her last outing suggests she's fit enough — but a mark of 81 and 151 lb to carry make the task harder for this consistent but elusive mare.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position by congestion at the rear — style-fit of 0.92 is the weakest natural fit here; Darragh O'Keeffe is a positive booking but form of P5-880 is uninspiring.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a pulled-up effort among them, Mother Ship faces questions about consistency, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 89 suggests some untapped ability; a trainer firing at just 5% lately is the concern.

runners_data.name: China Grill
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin is an eye-catching pilot but the form reads 0-000 on Good ground and the horse is a habitual fader allocated to midfield only because there is no room further back — STYLE_FIT discount is warranted.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last four starts, China Grill arrives here 32 days on from his latest outing carrying 150 lb, but remains lightly raced and unexposed — there is scope for improvement as connections look to find a way through.

runners_data.name: Drumadeise
runners_data.note: Consistent back-marker in terms of finishing position — four runs, all double-figure finishes on Good ground — pushed into midfield here but that does not reflect natural running style; a 7lb apprentice ride does not help.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, Drumadeise faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before, and 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but that's about as far as the positives stretch.

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Won on Good going over 16f recently and placed twice in similar company; mapped to midfield here though naturally a hold-up horse — the form is the strongest argument for a say, and Tom McGuinness has had a runner in the money recently.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two starts back makes him hard to trust despite a win last time out; he has run over today's going before, but ranked 14th of 17 on our figures and carrying 149 lb, there are significant questions to answer here.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Has placed from hold-up positions over 24f on Good ground, which is relevant; the redistribution note applies — he's not naturally a midfield horse — but he at least has the stamina for this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second four starts back shows she can threaten — her going experience and a quick 15-day turnaround keep her in the mix, but a rating of 77 and recent regression toward the rear make a big run hard to pin down.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Placed on Good going over 19f and wears a hood; PJ Rothwell has two other runners in this race and a 1/26 in-form trainer stat; natural hold-up runner mapped to midfield owing to field size, so take the map position with caution.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up and two single-figure finishes among them, Dark Berkshire is hard to fancy ranked 13 of 17 on our figures; a trainer in dire form at 1/26 over 14 days compounds the concern, though he does return quickly and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: Has shown modest form over 20-22f on Good ground but has pulled up last time out; tongue-tie and blinkers applied, PJ Rothwell stable, but a true hold-up type mapped to midfield — the redistribution is context, the form does the real talking.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up most recently, Little Boy Sivola arrives on a retrieval mission with a struggling yard — just one from 26 in the past fortnight. Has run over today's going, and 147 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Laligurash
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a form line of U-0780; a genuine hold-up horse in a field with too many of the same type — mapped to midfield but naturally will race further back; Going is fine but the form offers no real encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Laligurash has shown little in recent starts — unplaced last time out, with an eighth and seventh before that — yet to score in his last five, but the limited profile leaves plenty of questions unanswered and room to progress.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old top-weight who ran only yesterday, which is a serious concern regardless of other factors; hold-up profile, six career hurdle places suggesting he finds ways to get involved, but the turnaround time is almost unprecedented in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up two outings back is a concern, but General Clermont has distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 108 marks him a cut above this field despite a taxing 168 lb burden.

races.paceDynamic: Poppycon is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 17-runner field and should lead from the front under Joshua Halford, setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m4f on Good turf — nobody is likely to seriously challenge for the lead, so the fractions should be honest but not brutal. With only one horse genuinely committed to making the running, the race will settle into a procession through the early stages, with the large, bunched midfield tracking at a measured tempo before the pace lifts from three out. This shape — a single front-runner, controlled pace, race decided in the final half-mile — favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and pounce on the turn in, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close ground. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically operate from the rear in a single-pace race; Laligurash, Davitts Quay, Mother Ship, China Grill, Esticky End and several others are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the pack is simply too crowded at the back — of these, Esticky End and Ballinaboola Gold are most likely to actually secure a midfield berth given recent course form and trip suitability.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poppycon Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Poppycon leads at a fair but uncontested clip and the race is decided when the pace lifts turning for home.
scenarios.body: Poppycon dictates from the front without being pressed, leaving the race to be won by a prominent or tracking runner who sits within two lengths of the lead and pounces from the second-last; the lack of genuine pace pressure means hold-up horses stranded in the midfield pack arrive too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just quick enough that horses racing prominently drop away, and a genuine midfield tracker sustains a run from two out.
scenarios.body: The tempo proves slightly more taxing than anticipated, causing Poppycon to weaken inside the final flight, and a horse who settled third or fourth and travelled well sweeps through late; Larkins Lane, who has won twice over this trip, is the profile that benefits here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Defies Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than expected — perhaps Ballinvasas Best or another prominent type forces the pace — and a true hold-up runner gets a clear run through.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo stretches the field sufficiently to allow a closer to reel in the leaders in the final hundred yards; Esticky End, who has won and placed on similar going over shorter, is the most likely beneficiary of this scenario given recent form figures.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Descends Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 17-runner field produces interference, fallers or a bunched finish that scrambles the expected running order entirely.
scenarios.body: Traffic trouble at hurdles in a packed field can knock out the most fancied runners early; a horse who avoids incidents and finds a clear passage — regardless of style — takes advantage of the chaos, with General Clermont's experience at age 10 potentially seeing him through.

watchPoints.text: General Clermont ran just ONE day ago — monitor for any morning withdrawal or signs the 10-year-old is carrying fatigue into this race, as a horse racing on consecutive days over 2m4f is a significant risk factor.

With 17 runners, the large field creates serious traffic risk at every flight — watch for Laligurash, Drumadeise and China Grill, all habitual backmarkers who could find themselves squeezed out or knocked sideways in a bunched midfield.

Larkins Lane's chance depends entirely on getting a clear run from two out in a 17-horse race — any crowding at the second-last hurdle could end his bid before it begins despite the strong form figures.

Poppycon has a Fall in recent form (F in form string) — if the leader jumps poorly or makes an early jumping error, the entire race shape changes immediately as no other confirmed front-runner is present to take over.|

PJ Rothwell saddles three runners (Larkins Lane, Dark Berkshire, Little Boy Sivola) — watch for market moves on any of the trio at the off, as the stable may have a clear preference that the market will signal.|

runners_data.name: Baymount
runners_data.comment: Baymount has pulled up in each of her last two starts and was eighth three runs back, leaving her yet to win in recent starts; lightly raced and unexposed, she arrives fresh on 14 days' rest carrying 165 lb with more to offer if she can complete the course.

runners_data.name: Bredas Pearl
runners_data.comment: Bredas Pearl has run over today's trip and going, and a third last time out underlines her place-finding ability at a rating of 82 — the chief concern is her trainer's current run of 0/31 over the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Get It Girl
runners_data.comment: Get It Girl returns after a 295-day absence — unexposed and open to improvement — with a third last time out hinting at ability. She carries 165lb for a trainer firing at 28% in the last 14 days, and there's plenty more to discover from this lightly raced mare.

runners_data.name: Hartes Angels
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Hartes Angels returns after 53 days off and carries 165 lb on just her second start, yet to score but with scope to progress on that sole outing.

runners_data.name: Pat O's Rock
runners_data.comment: Debut mare carrying 165 lb, Pat O's Rock arrives completely unexposed with her slate blank — lightly raced by definition, she is open to any amount of improvement and represents a complete unknown with everything still to prove.

runners_data.name: Royal Tiara
runners_data.comment: Royal Tiara shaped with promise when third last time out, and she has experience over today's trip and going to call upon; winless in her last two starts, but carrying 165 lb, she looks the one to beat on her rating here.

runners_data.name: Shuil Solas
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score from her limited outings, Shuil Solas was fifth last time out and returns after 32 days; carrying 165 lb, she remains open to improvement with so little exposed about her.

runners_data.name: Slaney Valley
runners_data.comment: Slaney Valley makes her debut here carrying 165 lb, wholly unexposed and with everything still to learn — an open profile that leaves plenty of room for improvement on whatever she produces today.

runners_data.name: Vartry Diamond
runners_data.comment: Vartry Diamond makes her racecourse debut carrying 165 lb, with connections' yard finding winners hard to come by of late — just one from 26 in the past fortnight. Unexposed and open to any amount of improvement on debut.

runners_data.name: Fully Functional
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Fully Functional is yet to win in her last two starts — including a fall — but 75 days between runs and a stiff 162 lb burden make this a straightforward watch for what she shows next.

runners_data.name: Rathnaleen Aj
runners_data.comment: Unraced and unexposed, Rathnaleen Aj makes her debut carrying 162 lb — an unknown quantity with everything still to prove, but with no ceiling yet established she could be open to anything on her first start.

runners_data.name: Vadique
runners_data.comment: Vadique is unexposed and open to improvement — yet to score in her last two starts but shaped with promise when second two starts back, and 28 days between runs leaves her fresh enough to progress.
